# Masi App — Build Log

> **This is the master build log.** One file, the whole history: what was built, when, why, what
> broke, what was decided, and what was verified. It absorbed `sqlite-refactor-log.md` on 2026-07-13.
>
> **Where to append:** new work goes in the **Verification Register** (section 1) as a dated row.
> Decisions that will outlive the task go in the **Decision Register** (section 2). Bugs and gaps
> found along the way go in the **Bug and Gap Register** (section 3).

## How this log works

- **Append-only, newest at the bottom of each register.** Do not rewrite history. If something turns
  out to be wrong, correct it with a NEW dated row that says so.
- **A row is only worth writing if a future reader would be worse off without it.** Record: what
  changed, the exact verification (command plus result, with suite and test counts), review findings
  and how they were engaged, device checks, and anything surprising. Assumptions and dead ends are
  worth as much as successes.
- **Update this log after every meaningful work session**, especially anything touching the database,
  sync, or RLS. This instruction lives in `AGENTS.md` too.
- Related standing docs: `documentation/rls-sync-contract-map.md` (the RLS/sync contract),
  `documentation/ROADMAP.md` (what is still open and why it is ordered that way),
  `documentation/device-gates-sqlite-backend-2026-07.md` (what Jim still needs to check on a device),
  and `PRD.md` (the current product and architecture contract).

### History structure

The record spans two eras with two different shapes, both preserved as written:

| Section | Era | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Verification Register | 2026-05-19 to present | Dated table. **The live append target.** |
| 2. Decision Register | 2026-05-20 onward | Dated table: decision, rationale, revisit trigger. |
| 3. Bug and Gap Register | SQLite refactor onward | Dated table of bugs and gaps found. |
| 4. Narrative Timeline | June 2026 (Top-10 tranche: Items 3, 4, 8, 5) | Prose entries. |
| 5. Archive | SQLite refactor working artifacts | Point-in-time checklists, kept for provenance. |

| 2026-06-03 | Field preview build surfaced a stuck `letter_mastery` sync failure | Root cause found | Exported logs show the same record (`ff17e146-...`) failing `2026-06-02` and again `2026-06-03` with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_letter_mastery_unique_active"`; the Sync Status screen parks it in Failed Items with a Retry that re-fails. Root cause: `letter_mastery` is a logical-key-unique, push-only table that synced with a random per-device id (unlike `assessment_items`/`session_attendees`, which use deterministic ids), and `23505` is classified terminal. A fresh install over a backend that already held the EA's mastery (under old random ids) re-creates rows with new ids that collide on the logical-key index and stick forever. Decision (with Codex adversarial review): do NOT treat the duplicate as blind success (would leave local id ≠ server id and break later un-teach); instead canonicalize ids + adopt the server id. |

| 2026-06-16 | Sync-reliability slice (Top-10 Items 1+2): writer/reader split + outbox convergence | Implementation complete & Codex-converged; release gate green; **device pass pending (user)** | 12 TDD tasks on `fix/sync-reliability-writer-batch`; full per-task detail in `documentation/archive/sync-reliability-build-log.md`. Dedicated persistent SQLite **writer** (WAL, busy_timeout, FK-on post-migration) + read-only **reader** (`query_only`) — kills the per-call `withExclusiveTransactionAsync` connection-storm + pragma leak; `withTransaction` non-re-entrant by contract; all writes audited onto the writer. | 2026-07-14 | Deploy gate: re-key pre-fix assignment ids on `masi-app-sqlite` (26 rows) | Applied and verified; 0 mismatches remain across all five tables; test-EA fixture intact (9 children, 1 class, 7 groups) | Method: recompute each row's correct deterministic id **in SQL** (`uuid_generate_v5`, namespace `09dcf4b2-...`, parts joined by `chr(31)` — mirroring `deterministicDomainId`) and diff against the stored id. `letter_mastery` was **already clean** (13/13 current-formula v5), so that gate needed nothing. The other four tables held 26 landmines: `child_ea_assignments` 9, `child_programme_enrollments` 9, `class_ea_assignments` 1, `group_ea_assignments` 7. **The gate's original wording was wrong and would have caused a miss:** it said clean *"random-id"* rows, but all 7 `group_ea_assignments` rows carried valid **v5 deterministic** ids generated by a **superseded formula** (`group_id, ea_user_id, programme_id`; current `groupEaAssignmentDomainId` keys on `group_id` alone — confirmed by matching all 7 against the old formula). A cleanup filtering on "random ids" would have skipped every one and left the 23505 collision live. **The only sound test is whether the stored id equals what today's code computes for that row's logical key**, not whether the id looks random — with deterministic ids the derivation is part of the data contract. Fixed by re-key rather than wipe, deliberately: there is no seed script (the 2026-cohort script is unbuilt and `seed_data_plan.md` is schema-dead), so a wipe would have blocked the device gates behind building one. `child_programme_enrollments` has no identity trigger so a plain UPDATE sufficed; the other three have `prevent_assignment_identity_change`, which raises on `new.id is distinct from old.id` but fires on UPDATE only, so they were delete+reinserted inside one transaction preserving every other column (zero inbound FK references, verified). |

**Task 12 count and grade rules.** Assessed means a non-skipped `LETTER_EVIDENCE_CODES` result from
any recorder, standalone or battery, dated within the active academic year's inclusive
`starts_on..ends_on` window. Without an active year, count nothing. **Total is the number of such
letter-result rows for active children**, not distinct children or word tests. **Avg score** is the
rounded mean of each active child's latest qualifying raw letter score (no percent sign).
`getAssessmentCoverage` accepts typed results and an academic year; Home uses the explicit
`getCoverageFromCounts` helper on repository-qualified counts, with no shape sniffing.
`getAssessmentCountsSince` retains its name but no unused `sinceDate` parameter. Ranking grade uses
`[local enrollment day, local exit day)` via `toLocalDateString` in **Africa/Johannesburg**; the
move day belongs to the next class, with current-class grade as fallback. The timezone regression
covers a UTC timestamp crossing midnight in South Africa. History shows the recorder's standalone
rows and one read-only row per run, never separate battery-Question rows; detail uses stored items
and the stored set id.

### 2026-10-20 — Assessment Results Plan 1, Task 14 steps 1–2 (controller)

**Gate 1, local verification on `feat/assessment-results`.**
- `npx jest` (Node 20): **345 suites / 4,189 tests PASS**. `npm run test:types`: clean.
- All six PostgreSQL harnesses against the disposable PG17 on port 55432, `overall rc=0`:
  history-authorization, upload-contract, organisation-label, support-incident, ea-access, and
  assessment-results (**53/53 cases**, including both overlapping-retry cases).

**Gate 2, Codex adversarial review of the whole branch (`--base origin/main`), two rounds.**
- **Round 1, one high finding, fixed (`d66054b`).** Every package Question timed itself with
  `Date.now()`. A backward wall-clock correction mid-test produced a negative `duration_ms`
  (reproduced: −3,590,000 ms). `assertSubmitShape` refuses that, and Try again reuses the same
  result, so a finished test could never be saved. A forward correction ended timed tests early.
  - Root cause: Task 11 deleted `src/utils/monotonicClock.js` as unused, together with its
    regression test (`useAssessmentSession.clockJump.test.js`). The protection went with them.
  - Fix: `src/assessment-questions/progress/clock.ts` `monotonicNow()`, resolving
    `globalThis.performance` on each call, used for every elapsed time, deadline, stop or End
    freeze, and Undo shift in all 11 components. `duration_ms` is rounded to an integer.
    `performance.now()` is fractional, and a fractional value would also have been refused.
    `validateResult` now rejects negative, fractional and non-finite durations.
  - New `clockJump.test.tsx` covers backward and forward jumps for the letter test, the
    step-by-step word test and grid Q6. There is also a real-SQLite save of a stop-rule result
    after a backward jump. TDD RED was 12 failures.
- **Round 2: approve, no material findings.**
- **Also fixed by the controller (`fix(assessments)` commit).** History run rows took their date
  from the UTC day of `started_at`; they now use `toLocalDateString`. The regression test fails
  without the fix.

**Known risk, accepted (not fixed).** If the EA confirms Discard on the "This result isn't saved
yet" sheet while a save is already running, the screen leaves but the save still commits, so the
result is kept and uploads. The window is the few milliseconds of a local SQLite save. Ignoring
leave attempts mid-save would break the designed path where a save fails while that sheet is
open. Revisit only if it is seen in the field.

key by old `updated_at desc, id desc` before filtering. Keep only a synced winner; an unsynced
winner clears the entire key rather than resurrecting an older synced row. Drop unknown
languages and multi-character letters, and delete every old mastery outbox operation while
preserving unrelated work. Retained rows preserve old correction provenance, timestamps and
server-updated metadata; both new server-ordering fields start null. The JavaScript transform
then rewrites retained row IDs using UUID v5. Real SQLite proves transform failure rolls back the
rebuild, clear and version/ledger writes and restores FK enforcement, and relaunch performs no
writes.

**AR Plan 2 Task 3 — mastery repository and acknowledgement write-back.**

Replaced the old create/update/archive/reactivate methods with
`setLetterMastery({ childId, letter, language, confirmed, changedAt, programmeId, transaction })`.
Validation names the invalid field before any domain/outbox write. A call samples `Date.now()`
once, clamps a supplied tap time to that now, takes `changed_by` from the transaction's signed-in
EA, and mints a UUID v4 correction. A keyed joined read preserves a newer correction while its
slot is pending, failed or in flight; terminal/synced state and equal-time taps permit replacement.
A queued time ahead of the corrected phone clock counts as now, so a new immediate tap wins.
Retained calls return the mapped current record without exposing `outbox_status`.

A new write keeps `created_at` and all server metadata, clears the local error, marks the row
pending and queues exactly one `letter_mastery:<id>:update` slot with the nine-field payload.
Programme is supplied context or the caller's active Programme, possibly null, with no legacy
fallback. Real SQLite verifies one keyed read and two writes plus at most one Programme read;
a retained save reads once and writes nothing. Caller-transaction rollback and an outbox-trigger
failure both roll back the domain row and outbox together.

`getLetterMastery` maps `confirmed` to boolean, excludes terminal rows, rejects any `userId` or
`programmeId` key, supports child/language filters and 500-child chunks, deduplicates child IDs,
and orders combined rows by child and letter. `getUnsyncedRecords` remains available.
The named `applyCorrectionAcknowledgement` export implements all table branches. An applied
or superseded winner is written only after successful outbox deletion with a matching local
correction; superseded clears unknowable Programme context. A newer local correction keeps all
its content and slot and receives only server ordering. An acknowledged unreadable record is
deleted only when the same finalization conditions hold. Server timestamps remain raw strings,
including microseconds.

integration runner, and expanded to 30 tests covering the specified cases, every acknowledgement
table cell, the outbox CAS signal, transaction rollback, statement budgets and chunked read order.

**AR Plan 2 Task 4 — one RPC per correction, one acknowledgement.**

Added `letterMasteryCorrection.js`: six named RPC arguments, required-field/boolean/date
validation, and strict single-row acknowledgement parsing with only the five returned fields.
The raw server timestamp is preserved. The engine now routes mastery exclusively through
`set_letter_mastery`, maps local TypeErrors to `22023`, refuses malformed replies, and carries
the parsed winner and sent correction id into success finalization. Mastery is removed from
batchable upserts and archive/UPDATE-by-id routing; grant evidence is direct child delivery
assignment only. The server-column allowlist reflects current state, and the two server-ordering
columns are classified local-only.

Finalization applies Task 3's helper in the same transaction as the outbox CAS delete and normal
sync bookkeeping. A CAS miss applies only permissible server ordering before restoring the newer
slot to pending. Applied/superseded writes the returned winner; acknowledged removes a readable
copy that is no longer authorized; a newer local correction keeps its content and slot. A
content-update trigger failure rolls the delete and acknowledgement back together, then the
existing retry handler records failure/backoff without losing the correction.

**AR Plan 2 adversarial review round 2 — failed-save refresh recovery.**
The controller verified a failure-path gap in the round-1 fix at `c7b1d88`: a tap invalidated
an outstanding refresh, but a failed setter never scheduled a replacement read. The panel
could therefore retain a confirmation already removed in storage. A non-background focus
load completing while the write guard was held also discarded its loading cleanup, leaving
the spinner up permanently and hiding both the grid and the save error.

The replacement background read now starts in the setter's `finally`, after clearing the
write guard and pending-letter state, on both success and failure. A successful setter still
publishes its returned record; failure keeps the exact retry message. The newest read
converges with storage and clears loading, including when an earlier focus load was discarded.
Tap invalidation, read suppression during writes, invalidation by a later tap, the pending-write
guard, locked cells and success-only sync nudges remain intact. No existing mounted/cancellation
pattern exists in the panel; no new lifecycle machinery was added, as instructed.

Two regressions use the real SQLite mastery repository, with a native trigger rejecting the
confirmation of `m`. One holds a sync snapshot of `s` unconfirmed across the start of `m`'s
write, then rejects that write: the panel reloads `s` unconfirmed, retains the error, exposes an
enabled grid and completes an actual retry after the injected failure is removed. The other
delivers a non-background focus read while the write is pending, then rejects the write and
verifies the spinner ends and the error and retryable grid appear. The navigation test mock
now permits explicit focus delivery; storage and setter behavior remain real. All four round-1
regressions continue to pass. The standing contract map describes refresh after both outcomes.

#### Task 8: handle-owned store, trigger wiring and history trigger budget

`src/services/assessmentHistoryStatus.js`. The store waits for the signed-in handle's reference
readiness barrier and runs Battery Runs → assessments → mastery, with separate walker states,
page/run publication versions and per-walk results. `getPullStates(userId)` resolves that user's
active Programme scopes and unscoped mastery state; absent Programme values are null.
Missing identity starts do nothing. A returned cancellation stops the pass, other statuses
permit the next walk, and stale actor errors rethrow.

MR002 permits one reference refresh per pass and one rerun of the mismatched walk after a
successful refresh. Later/repeated mismatches never loop. The refresh is the real
`pullReferenceData(referenceOptions)` through the handle's refresh barrier, with current-actor
admission; it switches the local year whatever the response order (Task 7A). Ordinary refresh
failure logs the fixed tag and message only, leaves the walk incomplete and still allows
mastery. A stale refresh ends the pass. Tests execute this through the real reference
repositories and refresh in both response orders, including failed-year-query behavior.

is forced. This serial follow-up closes the class-persisted-after-coverage window without
starting concurrent walks. Reset invalidates all three walker states and all publication
callbacks, discards the pending pass (resolving its callers with null), and allows a new actor's
pass without waiting for the old actor. The snapshot remains generation-fenced through the old
pass's completion. No timer, schema, dependency or new automatic retry loop was added.

#### Controller adversarial review round 1: Retry convergence, tool hydration and year recovery

Addressed the three production failures reproduced by the controller on `25a901c`, with
real-SQLite RED regressions before each implementation change. No server migration changed.

**Finding 1 — terminal Retry could strand a synced wrong value.** A pull can replace the
displayed correction id while preserving the refused terminal payload. Successful finalization
therefore cannot require that displayed id to equal the sent id. `applyCorrectionAcknowledgement`
now installs the returned winner after the outbox CAS succeeds unless a pending/failed/in-flight
slot still carries a different correction. The latter, and an unsuccessful CAS, retain Plan 2's
ordering-only behavior. The existing direct CAS and newer-tap-mid-flight tests pass unchanged.
The history merge can also repair a synced display at an equal accepted tuple when its value,
actor, correction or time differs from its watermark. Owed slots still block every such merge;
consistent equal tuples remain no-ops, and terminal restoration retains refusal evidence.

The end-to-end local regression uses the real engine, Retry, walks and completeness accessor:
refusal → accepted-value pull restoration → successful Retry → immediate returned-winner
installation → next pull still equals the server, no outbox rows, completeness true. Separate
equal-watermark cases repair stranded correction/time and value-only mismatches.

**Finding 2 — a non-null tool FK could block every page retry.** The existing reference refresh
now fetches `assessment_tools` after programmes using its existing repository configuration.
The history store's readiness barrier awaits this refresh in the regression; both fresh and
previously completed caches acquire the active tool before the family/cursor commit. Its id
is retained. An explicit refresh runs even when the cache already completed, so no new marker,
schema, or fresh-install requirement was added. The existing signed-in provider also invokes
this full refresh (`src/context/SignedInEAContext.js:48-55`). Test adapters and reference fixture
maps now supply the eighth table.

#### Controller adversarial review round 2: cached co-EA assessment visibility at rollover

Fixed the verified round-2 finding on `8711be4`: a previously downloaded co-EA family remained
readable after the active academic year changed, even though the server's non-owner read arm
is year-bounded. **This is the plan's second and final adversarial review round; the two-round
review cap is reached.** No additional review round is implied by these local verification runs.

The canonical `getQuestionResults` now adds an owner/year predicate to every parent SQL
query, including `assessmentId` and chunked child/code reads. The reader's own `user_id` arm
has no implicit date bound. A non-owner row must satisfy an `EXISTS` on the active academic
year with inclusive `assessment_date BETWEEN starts_on AND ends_on`; no active year means
only owner rows remain readable. Explicit caller filters still narrow the query as before.
Item hydration receives only the visible parents. No post-filter or deletion changes cached
family data. `getLetterResults` inherits the rule, and the independent `countResults` SQL
aggregate shares the same private predicate.

Reader identity is explicit `userId`, or the bound handle id/registered SQLite connection
actor when omitted; without either it returns no results. The existing unscoped repository
test API therefore has no identity bypass. The sole production nested caller omitting an EA,
`batteryRuns.getRunWithResults`, now explicitly supplies the bound actor while retaining its
run-Programme override. It never uses the run recorder as reading authority. No signature changes.

#### Task 2 — local lesson draft repository

The factory-only `createLessonDraftsRepository({ database, idFactory })` exposes `getActive`,
`create`, `update` and `discard`, plus four named error classes and the pure `presentChildIds`
helper. Create/update use the existing repository transaction boundary. Context and a fixed plan
cannot drift; tracker changes retain their language code and ISO tap time; reading-level changes
contain edits only. Updates validate the complete merged draft and replace supplied JSON fields
whole. Unreadable JSON reports every affected column without changing the stored row. Discard
decodes nothing and joins an explicitly supplied save transaction, so a rollback restores the
draft with its original session id. No singleton, production caller, outbox row or server write
was added; handle wiring remains Task 3.

### 2026-10-22 — Wave-1 UI polish from the A03 device run

Fixed the six defects recorded on the Galaxy A03s (360 dp) on `fix/wave1-ui-polish`:

1. Class detail renders **Language: Not set** for null, undefined, empty or whitespace-only
   `home_language`; a nonblank language retains its original display value.
2. Class row metadata and `classRowLabel` drop null, undefined and blank parts before joining.
   Grade 1 / Ms Nolang / no language now reads **Grade 1 • Ms Nolang**, without a trailing
   separator or an empty spoken comma slot. Complete rows retain their existing text.
3. `SelectSheet` passes its null/undefined draft-key state to `BrandButton.disabled` and guards
   the confirm handler too. Pressing Start without a selection calls neither callback and keeps
   the sheet open; selecting an option enables confirmation. Audited every source caller:
   Assessment Child Select is the only SelectSheet with `confirmLabel`; the other confirm-label
   matches use ConfirmSheet. Immediate-selection sheets retain their behavior. Caller tests
   cover language choice, retained same-child drafts, another child's fresh draft and direct
   starts for recognized class languages.
4. The shared history walker retains an existing `lastFailureAt` and stamps wall time only
   when it is null/undefined. A successful page still clears it. The real-SQLite regression
   fails twice with a recreated walker between attempts, succeeds, then fails in a new streak.
   Reader audit before the change: `historyWalk` uses the marker to reject freshness and
   completeness; `pullCoverage` requires a null marker; the two sync-status presenters use it
   for the since label and choose the earliest incomplete walk. No reader requires the latest
   failure time. Session history and all three assessment/run/mastery configs delegate to this
   walker; there is no separate legacy session writer in this branch.
5. Both history presenters use one small timestamp formatter. Whitespace immediately before
   AM/PM (case-insensitive, dotted or undotted) becomes **U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE**. Tests supply
   ordinary whitespace, U+202F, tabs/newlines, dotted/lowercase variants, existing U+00A0 and
   24-hour locale text. No-meridiem text is unchanged.
6. **Review correction after 888416b:** the A03 adversarial review found three different
   stat-label sizes at 360 dp / 1.3x on Results, with Attempted and Incorrect shrinking below
   Correct. The review traced RN 0.81 Fabric Android's ignored `minimumFontScale` to the
   `minimumFontSize` conversion and TextLayoutManager's 4dp fallback. The original prop-only
   tests did not establish a native minimum size. Both screens now use
   `src/components/assessment/AssessmentStatCards.js`, with
   `stats: Array<{ key, value, label, accentColor }>` and the Results card metrics. Labels keep
   their caps, tracking and colour at the user's font scale; neither shrinking prop is set.
   The component first lays out an opacity-zero row and uses each label's full-size
   `onTextLayout` lines. All three one-line labels reveal the row; any multiline label selects
   full-width stacked cards, label left and value right. Container `onLayout` width changes,
   font-scale changes or changed labels remount the measuring subtree, so a later fitting
   measurement returns to the row. Stacked-label and late row callbacks cannot undo the row's
   wrap decision or leak into a new measurement pass. Each card is one accessible element
   announcing `<label>, <value>`; its child texts are not separate elements.

   **Round-2 review after c93132f (medium, accepted):** a missing or zero-line
   `onTextLayout` could leave all three cards invisible indefinitely; unchanged native
   measurements cannot be relied on to emit again. Each keyed generation now starts a
   1,000 ms deadline once width is positive. An undecided generation falls back to visible
   stacked cards at the deadline; zero lines stack immediately. Row and stack decisions are
   final within that generation. Decision/unmount clears the timer, late callbacks cannot
   change the decision or update an unmounted instance, and a new width/font-scale/label
   generation measures afresh. Reported Galaxy A03s build-28 evidence confirms events arrive:
   row at 411 dp / 1.0x; stacked at 360 dp / 1.0x and 411 dp / 1.3x, all statistics visible.
   This follow-up verifies the failure fallback with renderer/fake-timer tests; it performs
   no additional device run.

The sync contract map records the failure lifecycle and shared display formatter. No dependency,

### 2026-10-23 — EGRA follow-up: 60-letter minimum and story-questions auto-skip

After reviewing the integration, Jim decided:
- **Story questions auto-skip** when the child read no story words. Each EGRA battery now declares
  `prerequisites.reading_comprehension = { depends_on: 'oral_reading', minScore: 1 }`, which the
  existing `evaluateBatteryState` turns into a `skipped_prerequisite_unmet` auto-skip. A story
  with "Nothing attempted" scores 0, and a skipped story has no score; both trigger the skip.
  Persisting the skip is the Plan 3 host's job, as for every prerequisite.
- **Stronger skip rules later.** Letters 0 → no words or story. This is recorded on the roadmap,
  not built, because one dependency per Question can't express the full rule set.
- **The story first-line stop rule is wanted.** It needs printed line data the pack lacks
  (roadmap).
- **No Masi letter card under 60 letters.** The four Grade 1 forms (xh/en HL/en FAL/af, 40
  letters each) get 20 Masi letters appended. Selection rules:
  - 20 different letters, least-used first;
  - skip letters DBE leaves off both its Grade 1 and Grade 2 cards in that language (Afrikaans c
    and q, English HL q);
  - 10 capitals, preferring letters whose capital looks different;
  - a seeded shuffle with no repeated or easily confused neighbours.

  The selection script was run once, and its output is committed as data in
  `src/assessment-questions/egra/letterExtensions.ts`. The pack is untouched. Extended cards use
  version `<form id>-masi60`. The adapter rejects any future short card that has no extension.
  Resulting cards:
  - isiXhosa, English FAL: all 26 letters;
  - English HL: 25 letters (no q);
  - Afrikaans: 24 letters (no c, q);
  - at most 4 of any one letter, which equals DBE's own maximum on these cards.

  **Field consequence:** the printed DBE charts show 40 letters, so Masi must print 60-letter
  cards for these four forms before field use (roadmap).

Tests: adapter (extension identity, balance and neighbour rules, short-card rejection, the
prerequisite through the real `evaluateBatteryState`), gallery lookups by question version.

#### Review findings and fixes

- **Task 3 double-pull regression, caught during Task 7.** The first assignment publication
  scheduled a second full children pull on sign-in, credential recovery or reconnect. Task 7
  compares sorted notified class IDs with the last complete persisted roster's covered set,
  per handle/user. Notifications during a flight wait for its final coverage. Equal sets cause
  no second pull; uncovered grants get one follow-up. The four `task5AuthRaces` failures were
  introduced by Task 3, not pre-existing on `origin/main`. Both completion orders and a grant
  arriving during an older transaction are covered. Inconsistent grant-response fixtures and
  actor-mismatched archive fixtures were aligned without weakening assertions (`a333a62`).
- **Task 6 session-save skip.** A recently ended/non-delivery attendee's reading-level or mastery
  refusal could roll back the whole session. The persistence boundary catches only
  `NOT_DELIVERY_CHILD`, warns once per child, and continues. Session/attendee rows and authorized
  child/outbox writes still commit; other errors still roll back. Mixed-attendee and unrelated
  failure SQLite tests pin both paths (`3b9720f`).
- **Task 6 time-of-day test fixture.** Default “now” assignment timestamps could exceed a fixed
  archive time and violate `unassigned_at >= assigned_at`. Pinned fixture timestamps and
  `archivedAt = '2099-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'` remove that clock dependency without relaxing any
  guard or CHECK (`3b9720f`, [guard tests](../__tests__/nonDeliveryGuards.test.js)).
- **Accepted equal-version guard limit.** The saver rejects lower numeric versions on synced
  rows, but has no timestamp tie-breaker for equal versions. Missing versions also bypass the
  comparison; terminal rows keep their existing convergence behavior. An old equal-version open
  row can temporarily reopen a closed membership. This was characterized and accepted: a
  complete class/delivery reconcile can close the stale absent row, then replay can land the
  replacement (`bb63564`). This is eventual convergence, not a guarantee against every stale
  overwrite. The design and contract map record the qualification.

#### Review findings and fixes

- **onStart contract:** notify only on the first transition into capture, so the host can hide
  materials without altering capture behavior. Q2 chooses “I've finished reading” into marking;
  opening/closing its re-read sheet never reports a second start. Practice copy for Q3/Q4 stays
  in the intro; their Start begins capture. The sequential letter/word paths retain their
  existing callback owner. Contract coverage spans all eleven WelaPLUS Questions in EN/XH,
  re-read/review cancellation and completion. The rebased EGRA comprehension component also
  reports its start. Reducers, clocks and Result construction were not redesigned by this work.
- **Critical finalize Back loop:** Overview → Summary → finalize previously left a closed
  Overview beneath the summary; Back refocused it and replaced it with another summary.
  After successful finalize and a fresh committed read-only summary, `CommonActions.reset`
  removes every matching run's Overview below it, preserving unrelated routes and the summary
  key. Real-stack regressions cover Back, duplicate overviews, failed read/retry and
  `RUN_INCOMPLETE`, which still returns to the overview without pruning it.
- **Checklist border:** checked state retains both `backgroundColor: colors.primary` and
  `borderColor: colors.primary`. Only the run-code/child-name acknowledgment is required;
  no filing tick remains. It appears only for an eligible writable run with a Writing Sheet.
- **Overview refresh flash:** refocus retains the last rows instead of replacing them with a
  spinner. Start/actions stay gated while `data.refreshing`; Task 9 adds the deferred-read
  regression proving no navigation until the refreshed next Question is known. The summary
  uses the same first-load/refresh distinction.
- **Programme/roster authority:** screens wait for `getActiveProgrammeGate(...).programme?.id`
  and roster loading before treating `useAssessableChildren().all` as authoritative. Names
  come from that roster, then SQLite reference-name lookup. `buildRunView` owns writable and
  read-only reasons; a pulled run stays read-only and an unknown Battery has no capture path.
- **Save lifecycle:** `useGuardedQuestionSave` exposes `dismissSaveError` and keeps its queued
  navigation effect after `usePreventRemove` so the native-stack prevention state releases
  first. The Battery host uses the exact bundle object; fatal `RUN_NOT_WRITABLE` /
  `QUESTION_ALREADY_DECIDED` refuses retry, while successful save returns then requests sync.
- **Run races and completeness:** repository errors carry `error.code` and unfinished-run
  conflicts carry `error.runId`. The run guard uses non-throwing active-Programme lookup before
  resolution/duplicate checks, only on the Battery path. Start's unfinished check is scoped
  to user/child/programme, `in_progress`, `started_here = 1`. A selective NEW-outbox SQLite
  trigger proves abandon-and-start rollback after the old-run abandonment has executed.
- **History/EGRA display:** pulled runs open read-only summaries; standalone rows keep their
  original detail navigation. Done-row max is `derived.max ?? derived.questions_asked ??
  total_items`, so comprehension score 2 with three asked of five available displays `2 / 3`.
  The approved mixed-results expectation migration preserves its unregistered Battery fixture
  and all other assertions. EGRA registration remains owned by the EGRA team.

### 2026-10-25 — Story score: no default last word when marking mistakes

**Scope:** `fix/egra-story-last-word`, based on main `9708186`. Jim approved fixing it now, ahead of
the step-by-step capture redesign (which will move EGRA stories off tap-the-mistakes). Built by Codex
(`gpt-6.1-sol`, high), reviewed by Claude, then by an independent Codex adversarial review. Found by the capture-mode audit at main
`9708186` and verified by hand: EGRA `oral_reading` registers `ReadPassageQuestion` with
`markingPolarity: 'tap_wrong'`, but the last-item sheet defaulted to the highest tapped index
regardless of polarity. That index is the last mistake, not the last word read. With no mistakes,
the fallback was index 0: End → Confirm silently saved one attempted word. One mistake at word 6
silently saved six attempted words. The grid word path accepted the same polarity and had the
same defect, although no Battery currently combines grid capture and `tap_wrong`.

**Fix:** `LastAttemptedSheet.defaultIndex` now accepts `number | null`. A null default leaves
all tiles idle (no current ring or not-reached styling) and Confirm disabled and inert, exposing
`accessibilityState.disabled = true`. Choosing a tile enables Confirm and submits that index.
Both passage and grid callers pass null for `tap_wrong`; `tap_correct` retains the highest-marked
numeric default and index-0 fallback. Numeric selection/ring styling and accessibility labels and
state are preserved. Reached the end, Nothing attempted and Cancel retain their one-tap behavior.
No scoring formula, SequentialCapture, stepByStep, StopCard, story-questions, instructions or
WelaPLUS behavior changed; timer expiry still has no Cancel.

**RED → GREEN evidence (Node 20.19.4):** tests were added and run before the corresponding
production fix. The two EGRA cases and the host case each failed before changing the passage
caller; both grid variants failed before changing the grid caller. Regression tests for unchanged
behavior have no defect RED claim.

| New test | Before the fix | After the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Sheet: null default, idle tiles, disabled/inert Confirm, then tile → Confirm | `Expected "disabled": true; Received "disabled": false`; sheet run: `1 failed, 10 passed, 11 total` | PASS: no ring, all labels ink and unselected, Confirm inert, choosing item 3 submits index 2 |
| Registered EGRA: no errors, End at 30 s, choose word 20 | `expect(element).toBeDisabled()` failed: Confirm had `"disabled": false`; filtered run: `1 failed, 8 skipped, 9 total` | PASS: one completion, `ea_ended`, 30,000 ms, last index 19, 20 attempted/correct, 40 WCPM; items 0–19 correct and every later item not correct; `validateResult` valid |
| Registered EGRA: error at word 6, timer at 60 s, choose word 40 | `expect(element).toBeDisabled()` failed: Confirm had `"disabled": false`; filtered run: `1 failed, 9 skipped, 10 total` | PASS: no Cancel, one completion, `timer`, 60,000 ms, last index 39, 40 attempted, 39 correct, 39 WCPM; word 6 wrong and every later unattempted item not correct; `validateResult` valid |
| Host: real registered EGRA passage with letters/words already decided | `expect(element).toBeDisabled()` failed: Confirm had `"disabled": false`; filtered run: `1 failed, 81 skipped, 82 total` | PASS: Start → End → disabled Confirm saves nothing; choose word 20 → Confirm returns to overview and calls `saveQuestionResult` once with 20 attempted/correct |

### 2026-10-25 — Spec: step-by-step marking for every Question (`docs/step-by-step-capture`)

Field staff found WelaPLUS unclear after Question 1. "Leave blank for wrong", plus a finish sheet that fires
whenever a child gets anything wrong, made normal results look like EA mistakes. With Jim, designed one marking
method for every WelaPLUS and Full EGRA Question except the Q11 rubric:

- a ring on the current item;
- Correct / Incorrect / Back;
- tap-to-flip on marked items;
- a review step before Finish;
- an early end that leaves unmarked items "not reached".

Jim's decisions: Q9/Q10 keep their layout and step through it; Q6 stops after 10 wrong in a row; no "Not asked"
button; the passage goes word by word in both batteries (one method beats DBE tap-the-mistakes administration
for today's slow readers); a future passage method arrives as a server-assigned Battery version, never a switch.

Eight mockups were approved (`design/mockups-2026-10-step-by-step/`). Evidence sits beside the spec: a
16-agent read-only code map of all 13 Question components (`2026-10-25-step-by-step-capture-code-map.md`), and the
EGRA session's capture audit (`2026-10-25-step-by-step-capture-egra-audit.md`, 60 claims checked, 49
confirmed, 11 refined).

Surprises:

- WelaPLUS Q6's "5 in a row" stop is instruction text only.
- EGRA's passage counts untouched words as correct, and its last-word sheet pre-selects the last wrong word,
  saving an error-free reader as 1 word. That is fixed separately on `fix/egra-story-last-word`.
- Old and new results stay distinguishable without new content versions: toggle Questions save
  `capture_mode` null, and converted ones save `'sequential'`.

### 2026-10-28 — Leave sheet says what it does (#102)

Found in the Galaxy A03 device check on 2026-10-24 (build 39), and confirmed by reading the code
at `f095385`: the package End sheet saved `ea_ended`, while the host Back/✕ sheet discarded the
answers. Their titles differed by one word ("End this test?" / "End the test?"). The saving
sheet had a filled red action and the destructive sheet a quiet outlined action. Root cause:
two sheet components, one on each side of the package boundary, with near-identical titles
and inverted button weight.

Branch `fix/leave-sheet-102`, based on `561f668` (#114, the finish-flow change). Codex built
both rounds; Claude reviewed each diff, reran the focused gates and checked RED by restoring
the old screens. Round 1 was reviewed adversarially (`gpt-6-astra`, needs-attention, two
findings); round 2 below fixes both.

Jim chose **words + one look** (2026-10-28). The shared package `ConfirmPanel` is exported
from the package root. Both Question hosts draw it through the in-window `TestSheet` for leave,
save-error and closed sheets; package-owned sheets retain the native `ConfirmSheet` wrapper.
Leave says "Leave without saving?", names the child's answers or unsaved result (with an
empty-first-name fallback), and uses filled danger "Discard answers" / "Discard result".
"Keep marking" / "Keep result" cancel without changing the guard. Battery copy reassures that
finished questions stay saved. Save errors offer ink "Try again" and explicit "Not now";
closed assessments offer ink "Back to assessment", with hardware Back also closing them.

All original host visibility conditions are retained, including suppressing save errors while
leave is visible and, for a Battery, while closed. `TestSheet` takes an explicit `visible` prop
and renders nothing while hidden. The save guard now orders the leave decision before persistence
(see Review round 1). Package End copy/look, scoring and gallery behavior are preserved. Battery's
host `BrandButton` remains necessary for load-error retry outside the Question.

Original round 1 surprises / limits: before #102, the host used Paper Portal with a handle,

package's fading native Modal; the iOS handover finding below supersedes that choice. "Not now"
provides an explicit iOS escape from repeated save failures. One first-pass assertion counted

safe-area layout still require the **1.4.0 pilot build gate**; no separate build for this
copy-and-sheet change, and no device pass claimed here.

#### Review round 1

The adversarial review found two real defects in round 1:

1. **Native modal handover on iOS.** A host native Modal could mount while the package's End or
   stop Modal was still dismissing, or replace the leave Modal with save-error in one commit.
   UIKit can refuse that second presentation, leaving a finished Question with no visible retry.
   Extracted `ConfirmPanel` without changing its drawing or the package's native `ConfirmSheet`
   behavior. Only `ConfirmPanel` is public. Host `TestSheet` uses Paper Portal, never a native
   Modal, with the same panel and scrim, sheet-accessibility registration, title focus on an
   animation frame, consumed hardware Back, and a motion-token entry fade (none at `still`). It
   unmounts immediately on close. Paper moves children outside the app assessment-font provider,
   so `TestSheet` captures and forwards that existing font context inside the Portal. No timeouts
   were added.
2. **Discard could not stop a started save.** A timer completion during leave immediately started
   the repository transaction; Discard changed navigation flags but could not undo SQLite/outbox
   writes. The harm is permanent because EA results are immutable (ADR-0007). The hook now uses
   refs to make the leave decision and persistence mutually exclusive. Completion during leave
   retains the first result without persisting; Keep result starts the first save, while Discard
   writes nothing and ignores late completions. Back / ✕ / iOS back during a started save remains
   prevented without opening leave. Success navigates normally; failure offers save-error, after
   which leave/discard is truthful. Keep result after a failed attempt restores save-error rather
   than silently retrying. Native removal remains guarded until commit or explicit discard.

The initial vertical slices ran tests before the implementation: panel/export (3 failed), absent
host wrapper (module-not-found), deferred persistence (2 failed), Back during persistence (2 failed),
and native host Modal count (6 failed). Their green runs passed 14 panel cases, 3 initial host
cases, 6 hook cases and 6 focused host-screen cases. The expanded regression tests were then
replayed against round 1's hook/native-wrapper behavior, first together (26 failed / 119 passed),
then with focused filters in `/tmp/masi-102-red-replay` to avoid failure-reporting cascades. That
replay used `git show HEAD:src/hooks/useGuardedQuestionSave.js` (the hook was unchanged in round 1)
and the original native wrapper behavior, without changing the branch. The first
combined replay temporarily restored sources from in-memory copies in a `finally` block; all
later replay runs used the isolated directory. Expanded tests added after the vertical slices are
regression replay evidence, not a claim that every extra assertion was authored before its fix.

**Review round 2** (Codex `gpt-6-astra`, needs-attention, one finding, high): a completion queued
behind Discard re-armed the leave guard. `BatteryQuestionScreen` calls `guarded.onStart()` just
before `guarded.onComplete()` (`BatteryQuestionScreen.js:108`) so a timer completion is always
guarded, and `onStart` set `preventLeave` unconditionally. If Discard and a queued timer
completion landed in one batch, Discard scheduled `preventLeave=false`, `onStart` scheduled it
back to `true`, `onComplete` was ignored (`allowLeave`), and the pending discard navigation never
dispatched: the EA was left on an empty finished Question with Back and ✕ silently blocked. The
ordering predates round 2. Fix: `onStart` returns once `allowLeave` is set (saved, discarded or
fatal), since the screen is leaving in all three. Claude made this one-line fix directly, test
first: `useGuardedQuestionSave.test.js` "a completion queued behind Discard cannot re-arm the
leave guard" runs Discard, `onStart` and `onComplete` in one act before React commits (the
Battery order). RED: route names `['Entry', 'Question']` (stranded); GREEN: `['Entry']`, no
persist call. Gates after the fix (Node 20.19.4, run by Claude): focused 22 suites / 354 tests;
`npx jest` 435 suites / 6,675 tests / 14 snapshots; `npm run test:integration` 78 suites / 967
tests; `npm run test:types` clean; `npm run test:content` 5/5; `git diff --check` clean. The review loop stops
here: round 2's only catch was a narrow ordering race, now pinned by a test.

behind the failure barrier". The screen preserves the chosen tier if its child returns; it displays
the default while the tier is absent. `useLessonDraft.beginSave` queues the correction and blocks

session after a failed correction and the displayed tier plus retained ticks after retry. This is
current behaviour, superseding rounds 3–4's automatic-reset mechanism. Review round 6 approved it.

the write to the one place it matters, Save, where the existing failure barrier already gives the
guarantee.

**Code review round 1 (Codex, gpt-6-astra): one medium finding, reproduced.** Splitting the base
load (sessions) from the participant load (session-history completeness) let the two come from
different moments. Open a lesson while past lessons are still downloading (no sessions, history
incomplete); the download finishes with an earlier lesson for an attendee; add a child. The
participant load now reads history as complete, the base still has no sessions, the engine
infers `first_session`, and the first tick freezes that plan. Fix (Codex built, Claude
reviewed): the base reads session-history coverage **before** the sessions and carries both
(`sessionHistoryCoveredChildIds`); the pull writes pages and cursor in one transaction, so the
sessions read afterwards are at least as new as the coverage claim. `presentLessonInput` takes
each child's `historyComplete` from that coverage, and mastery completeness is read before known
letters for the same reason. The hook's base key includes the session-history store's
`pageVersion` and `runVersion`; a refresh keeps the shown base, plan and choices until the new
base lands, and an unfrozen same-day plan then follows it. Codex's first patch also recomputed a
resumed plan on mount (caught by the midnight save test; narrowed). Claude added: a failed
background refresh keeps the shown suggestions and logs, instead of showing "Couldn't load" over
working suggestions. The picker uses the same coverage (ranking 6 statements). Committed `96da985`.

**Code review round 2 (Codex, gpt-6-astra): one high finding, reproduced.** Round 1's fix let any
refreshed base recompute a stored unfrozen plan, through a `refreshed` flag each hook kept for
good. Lesson stays mounted under Wrap up, and each screen loads its own facts, so the two can
hold different mastery completeness. After one history refresh each screen computed a different
plan and overwrote the other's through the shared draft controller, forever. Our test of the
reviewer's scenario ran Node out of memory on that code. Fix (Claude): a stored plan is replaced
only by an attendance change (as before) or by inputs at least as complete on both counts and
more complete on one (`isPlanSuperseded`, pure, in the engine). Both tests read the stored plan,
so whichever screen writes first settles it for the other: at most two writes, and a fall in
completeness never writes. Two hook copies with different facts now converge in 2 distinct
writes; a refresh that adds nothing leaves a resumed plan alone. Measuring writes needs care: the
controller runs each transition about three times per write (check, optimistic view, save), so
counting `setPlan` calls reads 6 for 2 writes; the test counts `controller.apply` calls instead.
Committed `1d2eda1`.

**Code review round 3 (Codex, gpt-6-astra; the last round): one medium finding, reproduced.**
Round 2's rule ends when writes succeed, but a failed automatic plan write retried without end.
The controller drops a failed write and republishes the stored plan; the screen still sees that
plan as superseded, so it writes again. On a phone whose storage fails (a full disk), a resumed
lesson churns SQLite and React with no one touching it. Our test (Lesson and Wrap up both
mounted, every draft update failing at the native adapter) hung on that code. Fix (Claude, one
condition): the automatic write waits while the controller holds "Couldn't save your last
change", which only a successful write clears, so the upgrade follows the EA's next change. Now
at most 2 failed attempts, then the next change stores the upgrade. A second change, Save adding
the plan on screen when it differs from the stored one, was built and then removed by the
simplicity check below. **Accepted known risk:** a Save with no ticks straight after a failed
upgrade records the older plan, with its own completeness flags; any tick already stores the
plan on screen. Rounds found 1, 1 and 1 issue, each with one fix; round 3 was the last.
Committed `dea72c6`.

**Simplicity check (`check-solution`, because the finding count stopped falling).** Coverage read
before sessions: keep (the picker and the lesson both use it). History refresh: keep (an
untouched lesson's suggestions and its "Still downloading past lessons" note update when history
lands). Upgrading a stored unfrozen plan, with its failure gate: keep, because `LessonScreen`
shows that note from the stored plan's `history_complete`, so without the upgrade the note stays
after the download ends; `isPlanSuperseded` is the smallest rule found that stops. Save adding
the plan on screen: removed, since no one can tell which of two consistent plans a no-tick record
holds.

**Verification.** Host load averaged 40–130 during the session (other sessions' Jest runs), and
parallel runs timed out in unchanged suites; every such suite passed serially. Final gates on
`dea72c6`: unit **411/411 suites, 5,920 tests** (`--maxWorkers=25%`); integration **82/82
suites, 1,127 tests**; `npm run test:types` clean. Earlier: `96da985` 410 / 5,905 and 82 / 1,127;
`1d2eda1` 411 / 5,919 and 82 / 1,127.

- **Discovery findings that shaped the plan** (verified across Masi + fork `c183d3e`):
  - **Save path is an impedance layer, so the hook stays schema-agnostic.** `assessmentsRepository.saveAssessment`
    takes the screen's "fat" record and itself injects `programme_id` (NOT-NULL, via `resolveProgrammeId`), maps
    `date_assessed→assessment_date` / `correct_responses→score` / `letters_attempted→total_items`, and splits the EGRA
    detail into the normalized `assessment_items` table (`__summary__` row + per-letter rows). The extracted hook just
    rebuilds the same fat object + `capture_mode`; **no repo-internals surgery.**
  - **`capture_mode` is a 3-file code contract**, not one: local migration (`src/db/migrations.js` v4) **+**
    `ASSESSMENT_COLUMNS` (`assessmentsRepository.js`) **+** `SERVER_COLUMNS` (`src/services/offlineSync.js:195`) — miss
    the last and it persists locally but never syncs — **+** Supabase migration **+** contract map **+** refactor log.
  - **Column is nullable, NO DB default.** `NULL = legacy/grid`; a `DEFAULT 'sequential'` would mislabel grid rows
    written by older field app versions → corrupts the A/B. Client stamps the resolved mode explicitly.
  - **`correction_count`** rides in the existing `__summary__` metadata JSON (one line in `buildSummary`) → **no extra
    migration.**
  - **Three** assessment entry points exist (not two): `AssessmentChildSelectScreen:73`, `ChildAssessmentSummaryScreen:117`
    ("Run Assessment"), `AssessmentResultsScreen:34` ("Try Again").
  - `EgraLetterGrid` lacks `readOnly`/`currentIndex` (only `disabled`, which dims) → Task 9 adds them backward-compatibly.
  - CONTEXT.md already defines **"marking mode"** (who scores) → plan adds a **"capture mode"** glossary entry to prevent
    drift (orthogonal axis: which UI mechanic).

     no-op seams). No new write path to the read-only `users` table. Default = `sequential`.
  2. **"Try Again" routing deferred to Item 5.** Route only the two clean entry points now;
     `AssessmentResultsScreen.handleTryAgain` keeps launching the grid until Item 5 (which owns that screen + has
     unrelated uncommitted edits there) routes it. **Disclosed gap, not silently dropped.**

#### Task 17 device gate and final fix round (2026-10-22)

Final whole-branch adversarial review (Codex gpt-6-astra, `--base origin/main`, 21 commits):
one Important finding — Q6's Previous/Next page updates were unclamped, so two queued taps could
leave the pages array and blank the grid while the timer ran. Frozen engine files
(`stepByStep.ts`, `clock.ts`, `applyProgress.ts`, `Result.ts`) were unchanged and 22
Result-equivalence scenarios (all 11 Questions, en + xh) matched origin/main.

Device: Samsung A03s SM-A037U, Android 13, `wm density 320` (360dp wide), 3-button navigation,
EAS preview APKs. Build 29 (`a3d4274`) for the first pass; build 30 (`76d6289`) and build 31
(`19fea62`) to re-verify the fixes. Screenshots stayed in the controller's scratchpad.

Passed on build 29 and still passing: letter pages of 5 × 20 with the dashed card-row divider;
ink ring on the current tile; green/red marks; Back across a page edge (page 2 → page 1 with `v`
refocused and unmarked); a stop on page 2's last tile keeps page 2; timer amber at 9s; End sheet;
bottom bars clear the 3-button bar; font scale 1.3 (grid fits, intro/sheets reflow); the gallery
appears on the embedded preview build; all nine WelaPLUS Questions in English and isiXhosa,
including the fixture rubric sheet, Q5 picture tiles and the Q2 re-read sheet; Q5 Next clamp.
**I/l:** Andika draws capital `I` with serifs and lowercase `l` as a plain stem — clearly distinct —
so the three `typeface` content items (letter_sounds@2026.2 en/xh/af) are closed.

Found on device (none visible to Jest) and fixed in `76d6289`:

| Finding | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The focused letter/word shrank (`ibhulukhwe`, `umnqwazi`, even `l`), then grew back once marked | `current` used a 3dp border vs 1dp elsewhere; the 4dp lost from the content box tipped Android's `adjustsFontSizeToFit` with Andika's tall line box | Every state keeps a 1dp border; the 3dp ring is a decorative overlay outset over it (`ui/MarkTile.tsx`) |
| Q8 timer label "59s" clipped (en + xh) | `TimerBar` row had `flexShrink: 1`; a long passage squashed it. Q6's short content hid it | `flexShrink: 0` (`ui/TimerBar.tsx`) |
| Short pages floated mid-screen; tiles jumped ~150dp between pages (Q5 page 3, every Q6 page) | `PagedGrid` sized tiles from the visible page's own row count | One frame from the Question's largest page; short pages fill it from the top (`ui/PagedGrid.tsx`) |
| Q5 isiXhosa letters misaligned when a caption wrapped ("ufudo (tortoise)") | Caption height followed its line count | Two-line caption box × min(OS font scale, 1.2) |
| Stop card / End sheet left the host header and ✕ bright and tappable; no hardware Back | ConfirmSheet was an in-tree overlay (same on main) | ConfirmSheet renders in a transparent Modal; Back cancels, or does nothing on the stop card |
| A stopped test still ringed the next tile | Tile state ignored `stopped` (same on main) | No current tile while stopped; Undo restores it |
| Q6 pager at the top, Q5's in the bottom bar; Q2 started 8dp below the header | Placement left to the builder | Q6 controls move into the bottom bar; Q2 gets the standard top padding |

Build 30 then showed a new defect: the Modal ConfirmSheet's panel sat under the 3-button bar,
because the implementer dropped the Android bottom inset on the assumption that an Android Modal
excludes the navigation bar. Under Expo SDK 54 the Modal is edge-to-edge. `19fea62` restores
`max(useBottomInset(), 24dp)` on both platforms; build 31 shows Save result / Undo last mark and
End test / Cancel clear of the bar. Hardware Back verified: it cancels the End sheet and leaves the
stop card in place.

### 2026-10-27 — EGRA content and skip rules: skip card at large text

The Galaxy A03 device pass on build 51 (`a9d4141`, 360dp) found the skip card's two side-by-side
lists too narrow at Samsung's 130% text: "Story comprehension" broke mid-word as "Story compreh /
ension" in the Skipped column. The sheet also reached its 80% height, and the body scrolled with
nothing showing that four more titles sat below the fold. At 100% text the card was correct.

Measured on the 100% screenshot, "comprehension" is 193px (about 97dp) in `textSmall`. A 152dp
column leaves 128dp for text, and the word needs about 125dp at 130%, so Android broke it.
`SkipNoticeSheet` now gives each list `flexBasis: 136dp × fontScale` inside a wrapping row
(`flexGrow`/`flexShrink: 1`). On a 360dp phone the lists stay side by side up to about 110% text and
stack above that. The footer keeps no rule while the body fits. When the body scrolls (body content
taller than its viewport, from the ScrollView's `onLayout` and `onContentSizeChange`), it shows the
standard `BottomSheet` footer rule. `BottomSheet` gains a `bottom-sheet-footer` testID only.
`design-system.md` describes the wrap and the rule, and now gives the footer's real 24dp top
padding (`spacing.lg`) where it said 16dp.

TDD: three new cases in `__tests__/SkipNoticeSheet.test.js` failed first (missing test IDs and
behaviour), then passed. The 100% and 130% cases pin the wrap rule (Jest has no layout engine; the
A03 proves the result). The scroll case drives `onContentSizeChange` and `onLayout` and expects the
rule only while content outgrows the body. The test reaches `useWindowDimensions` through
`require('react-native')`: a spy on an `import * as` namespace copy never reaches the component.

| Command (Node 20) | Result |
|---|---|
| `jest __tests__/SkipNoticeSheet.test.js` before the change | 1 suite failed: 3 failed / 4 passed |
| `jest __tests__/SkipNoticeSheet.test.js __tests__/BottomSheet.test.js __tests__/BatteryOverviewScreen.test.js` | PASS: 3 suites / 98 tests |

Left for follow-up, outside this branch:
- `BottomSheet` pads its bottom with `max(safe-area inset, 24dp)`. On Android's three-button bar the
  inset equals the bar, so every sheet's footer sits flush against it, and the skip card's Got it
  shadow is cut. iPhone needs checking alongside.
- `ListRow` subtitles wrap greedily. "Letter writing first row wrong" leaves "wrong" alone on a
  second line at 360dp/100%. `textBreakStrategy="balanced"` (Android) would fix it app-wide.

   changes accordingly (the only one of 13 that moves); answer guides are EA-facing text and are not
   stored in results.

### 2026-10-27 — English letters on DBE FAL 3; quick-test result text; docs drift from the EGRA review

The EGRA session's full review of #108 found the code correct and left content questions, two
small results-screen bugs and doc drift. Jim chose (2026-10-27): fix the results screen and the doc
drift in one PR without a device build, and fix the English letter chart, not Letter mastery.

**English letters.** DBE English Home Language Assessment 3 has 100 letters but only 22 distinct:
no q, v, x or z (counted from `content/egra/egra-assessments.json`). Letter mastery reads a child's
latest letter result, so an English child's tracker would have dropped to at most 22 of 26 after
one 2026.3 assessment. Of the pack's charts, English FAL 3 is the only 100-letter English one with
all 26 (19 upper case, practice items `d h v`). `SHARED_READING_FORMS.en.letters` now points at
`dbe-egra-en-fal-3-v1`, changed in place at 2026.3: nothing was printed and no field results
existed. Saved results keep their own prompts, so the few English staging test results still read
correctly. isiZulu's SMRS chart has no `r` and stays as printed (Jim). A new test checks every
shared chart asks all 26 letters except isiZulu `r`. The printout pack's English side A is
regenerated from the pack data and names the FAL booklet (`egra-efal-guide.pdf`, PDF page 15).

**Quick-test results screen.** It said "Stopped: 10 in a row wrong" for every stop, but since #108
the quick tests stop when the whole first row is wrong (8 words in English, 5 in isiZulu). The text
now follows the saved item set's own rule: "Stopped: the whole first row was wrong" on 2026.3,
"Stopped: 10 in a row wrong" for older results. Its praise came from accuracy over the items read,
so a child who read one word correctly heard "Excellent work! 100% correct". Praise now follows the
child's score band (`getScoreBand`, the same bands as the rankings; grade from the roster child).
Word Reading has no bands yet, so it gets no praise, like its neutral ranking, and the accuracy line
reads "N% of attempted correct". "Nice try!" (accuracy 40–59%) has no band and is gone.

**Docs.** `CONTEXT.md`: the `-masi60` extension matters only for finishing an unfinished old Grade 1
assessment (verified: outside capture the item-set lookups serve only answering or skipping a
Question in an unfinished run, the dev gallery and the new stop text). The spec gets dated
corrections. `PRD.md` §6.7 (four quick-test languages; no last-attempted confirmation) and §7.3
(wired). Dated status notes on the WelaPLUS agent briefing, the WelaPLUS PRD, the July SQLite device
gates and the content-pack plan. `egra_letter_sets.md` no longer asks for real word lists.

administration rules, per-minute scores, source-note decisions, isiXhosa practice items) and

### 2026-10-27 — Letter tracker keeps each letter's newest evidence; shared EGRA pack restored

Branch `fix/letter-evidence-pack-restore`, from main `92a27b8` (#112). Raised by another agent after
#112; Jim chose to land both before the TestFlight pilot is cut, so no extra build.

**Letter tracker.** Assessment evidence used only the child's latest letter result, so any letter
that result did not reach was wiped: a chart that never asks it or a child who runs out of time.
Letters each pack chart never asks (checked from the pack): isiXhosa HL 1 c i o p, HL 2 j; English
HL 1 q, HL 2 o q v x z, HL 3 q v x z; English FAL 1 q x; Afrikaans HL 1 and 2 c q; isiZulu SMRS r;
isiXhosa HL 3, English FAL 2 and 3 and Afrikaans HL 3 ask all 26. On
English FAL 3, q first appears at letter 22, z at 27 and x at 31, so a child reading 25 letters in
the 60 seconds lost z and x even after #112. Now each letter takes its status from the newest
eligible result that reached it (`computeLetterMastery` over `eligibleLetterResults`, newest first);
a newer wrong answer still un-masters it. The tracker (`loadMasteryState` through the new
`assessments.letterEvidenceFor`, which replaces `latestLetterResult`) and the ranking share the same
functions; "Last assessed" still shows the newest letter result. No schema, sync or RLS change.
Consequence: chart choice no longer affects the tracker, so English HL 3 vs FAL 3 is now a teaching
choice (roadmap).

**Shared EGRA content pack.** #111 removed a stray `”` from `dbe-egra-xh-hl-1-v1`'s question 4 answer
guide in place. The pack is byte-identical across both apps and both websites, its README lists
that quote as retained from the DBE source, and a corrected form must get a new form id. The edit
made `npm run test:content` fail on main (hash `a93275dc…` instead of `ce3f99d7…`), and CI never ran
that check. Restored the JSON and the adapter baseline snapshot to the pre-#111 bytes; #111's quote
test now records that one source exception; CI runs `npm run test:content`. A fix to the quote
comes from the pack's owner as a new form id. Not changed: Afrikaans 2's chart says 60 but prints
70 letters, already recorded in the pack README as visually checked, and no new assessment uses it.

Docs: `CONTEXT.md` (Letter mastery), `rls-sync-contract-map.md` (current-year letter evidence),
`egra_letter_sets.md`, `ROADMAP.md` (letter evidence, source notes, chart switching).

TDD: six new unit cases (26 letters then the real HL 3 chart still 26; FAL 3 with 25 letters read
keeps x and z; a newer wrong answer un-masters and a newer right one masters; date then creation
time decide; skipped, other-language and other-child results give nothing; no results) and one
real-SQLite tracker/ranking case failed first, then passed. One ranking expectation changed by
design (2 → 3: the older results now supply `a`). Tracker mocks moved to `letterEvidenceFor`.

Gates (Node 20): `jest --silent` 434 suites / 6,624 tests / 14 snapshots; integration 78 suites /
967 tests; `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.assessment-questions.json` clean; `node --test
content/egra/verify.cjs` 5/5. No device build (Jim).

Review: Codex adversarial review (`gpt-6-astra`, base `origin/main`): approve, no material findings
(its sandbox could not write the Jest cache, so it probed the functions directly; the suites above
ran locally). It noted a consequence to keep in mind when reading the pilot: "Last assessed" is the
newest letter result, not the date each mastered letter was last seen. A child with all 26 in March
who gets the whole first row of FAL 3 wrong in October keeps the 16 letters October did not reach.

### 2026-10-28 — Assessment finish: Finalize on the overview, then the next child

**Jim's notes on iOS build 24 (Full EGRA, Anke Afrika, Afrikaans).** "Review and finalize"
opened a second screen that listed the same Questions again just to show Finalize. After
Finalize that screen turned read-only ("Assessment summary", Finalized) with no footer, so the
EA was stuck with only the header back arrow. Both WelaPLUS and Full EGRA use these screens, and
the 1.4.0 pilot (#110) ships main, so the dead end would have reached pilot testers.

**Jim's choice (2026-10-28): one screen, then the next child.** This restores the WelaPLUS spec's
original §5.3 intent ("Once every Question is decided, Finalize run is enabled" on the overview).
- The overview's footer offers **Finalize assessment**. When the battery has a Writing Sheet, the
  existing check ("Write assessment code … on the Writing Sheet") sits after the Question list, and
  Finalize stays disabled with "Tick the box to finalize" until it is ticked. Finalize uses the
  overview's mutation guards, requests sync and replaces the overview with the summary
  (`{ runId, finalized: true }`) straight after the committed write. `RUN_INCOMPLETE` reloads;
  other errors show "Couldn't finalize this assessment. Try again."
- The summary is read-only and always titled "Assessment summary". Opened straight after Finalize
  it offers **Assess next child** (to the child picker for the same battery, when that battery can
  still start new runs) and **Back to Assess**. Opened from history it has no footer.
- History opens unfinished runs (stored `in_progress`; "Open" is only the badge) on the overview,
  so they can still be finished. Without this, moving Finalize would have stranded them on a
  read-only summary.
- The skip card ends "Tap Finalize assessment to finish."

**Build and review.** Codex built it test first. The first run stopped before editing because the
work order said `status === 'open'`; the stored value is `in_progress`. The order was corrected
and rerun. RED: 4 suites, 34 failing tests (no Finalize on the overview; history still opening
the summary; old skip copy), plus the navigator title test. The summary's finalize tests moved to
the overview, and new ones cover the finish footer, an unavailable form and Back after the
replace. Gates (Node 20): `npm test` 434 suites / 6,636 tests (Codex); the six affected suites
(236 tests) and `npm run test:integration` (78 suites / 967 tests) rerun by the orchestrator;
`npm run test:types` clean; `node --test content/egra/verify.cjs` 5/5. Specs updated in the same
change: WelaPLUS Release 1 §5.4 (dated note), EGRA content and skip rules (copy), design-system
(the check now sits on the overview). Device check: next build.

Review: Codex adversarial review (`gpt-6-astra`, base `origin/main`) of `65b36af`: approve, no
material findings. It confirmed the overview's mutation guard blocks repeated taps; the
repository's finalize transaction refuses closed, remote or incomplete runs; and the replace runs
before the overview's closed-run redirect can fire. Unfinished runs stay reachable from history
and the Assess list, and Home and child results add no stranded summary route. Its probes also
exercised what the unit tests mock: "Back to Assess" selecting the Assess tab through the nested
`popTo`, and "Assess next child" for all 16 registered battery identities. Its sandbox could not
write the Jest cache, so it ran those probes with caching off; the suites above ran normally here.
Open: the native smoke check (Writing Sheet tick, rapid Finalize taps, Back from the summary,
both footer buttons) on the next build.
